CHAPTER 3
Preparation of Gases General Idea about the Preparation and Collection of Gases in the Laboratory Selection of apparatus
a) The gases which are prepared by the application of heat are
prepared in a hard glass test tube or round bottom flask.
b) The gases which are prepared without the application of heat
are prepared either in a Woulfts bottle or in a conical flask.
Simple reactions are carried out in a Woulfs bottle and whereas vigorous reactions are carried out in a conical flask.
c) Dropping funnel is used if the liquid has to be added in small
lots or if the reaction is vigorous, otherwise thistle funnel is used to pour the liquid.
Collection of gases
a) Water soluble gases are collected by displacement of air. If the
gas is heavier than air, it is collected by upward displacement of air and if the gas is lighter than air then it is collected by downward displacement of water.
b) Water insoluble gases are collected by downward displacement
of water. They are lighter than air. Note: A gas is preferred to be collected in water because while collected in air, it mixes with air to some extent.
Fitting of apparatus: While fitting the apparatus, you need simple skill for cutting a glass tube, bending a glass tube through different angles and boring a cork.
Practical Chemistry
a) Cutting a glass tube: When you need to cut a glass tube then

follow the steps given below. i) Put the glass tube on the edge of your working table and hold it with your left hand. ii) Give a mark at the point of the glass tube where you Want to cut. Take a triangular file in the right hand and make a single deep scratch on the mark by drawing the file towards yourself. iii) Do not move the file back and forth. If one operation is not sufficient to make a deep scratch, you can draw the file again in the same way at the same place. iv) Place the thumbs on either side of the scratch with the scratch facing outwards. v) Break the tube by pulling gently towards yourself. vi) The broken tube has sharp edge. Make this sharp edge smooth by heating the edges in the oxidising flame (nonluminous flame) and allow it to cool on the asbestos sheet.

b) Bending of a tube (Making a delivery tube)

i) Hold the tube lengthwise with both hands along the nonluminous flame and heat the part of the tube where you want to bend with constant rotating. ii) When the tube gets soft enough to be bent by its own weight, quickly place it on the asbestos and bend into the desired angle without applying force.
